channel.title: Mitesh Gandhi | Reflections
channel.description: Weekly reflections from an optometrist on the art of seeing, and being seen.

item.title: From the quiet son to live on BBC Radio
item.description: BBC Radio Cambridgeshire, 2019, live. If you'd told my younger self, the quiet son who never spoke up, he'd have laughed. So what changed?

item.title: The tree of life in the eye
item.description: Every day I look into the eye and see an optic disc, branching vessels, a cross behind the eyes. Science explains the how. Meditation lets me wonder at the why.

item.title: A stranger on a mountain gave me the keys to my life
item.description: I was 23, sitting on a mountain in India, and I had never lived away from home. Then a stranger asked me a question that quietly changed the rest of my life.

item.title: The letter that took me back to 1986
item.description: This week, a handwritten letter arrived from a patient. As I read it, I was back in our living room in 1986, watching my grandma cry.

item.title: For most of my childhood, I wanted to disappear
item.description: At four years old, white patches began to appear around my eyes and across my body. Today I spend my working days looking into people's eyes, and I've learned that looking and seeing are not the same thing.
